title: Catch more spam, pay for it
hook: Lowering the bar catches more spam. What else does it catch?

knows: that a model can give each email a score
doesNotKnow: that a score threshold trades one kind of mistake for another

misconception: Catching more spam is simply a better filter.
objective: The learner can explain that when scores of two classes overlap, moving the threshold trades missed spam for false alarms, and that choosing the threshold is a decision about which mistake costs more.

claims.text: The toy has ten invented emails with spam scores: spam 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3; real mail 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1. Mail scoring at or above the threshold is flagged.
claims.source: The lesson's own data in Demo.tsx (SPAM, REAL, counts()).

claims.text: At 0.50, 4 of 5 spam are caught and 1 real email (0.6) is flagged. At 0.25, all 5 spam are caught and 3 real emails (0.6, 0.4, 0.3) are flagged. At 0.65, no real mail is flagged and 2 spam get through.
claims.source: Count the scores at or above each threshold. Reproduced by running counts() from Demo.tsx: t = 50 → 4, 1; t = 25 → 5, 3; t = 65 → 3, 0.

claims.text: The lowest-scoring spam (0.3) is below real mail at 0.6 and 0.4 and level with one at 0.3, so no threshold catches all spam without flagging real mail.
claims.source: Catching the 0.3 spam needs threshold ≤ 0.3, which also flags real mail at 0.6, 0.4 and 0.3.

claims.text: Recall is spam caught ÷ all spam; precision is spam flagged ÷ all flagged. Going from 0.50 to 0.25, recall goes 4/5 → 5/5 and precision 4/5 → 5/8.
claims.source: Manning, Raghavan & Schütze 2008, Introduction to Information Retrieval, Cambridge University Press, §8.3 (definitions); values from counts() in Demo.tsx.

recall.question: A cancer screen flags anyone whose score is above a cutoff. Doctors lower the cutoff. What should they expect?
options: More cancers caught and more healthy people flagged
More cancers caught, nothing else changes
recall.why: When scores overlap, a lower cutoff reaches more true cases only by also reaching more false ones. The cutoff picks which mistake you accept.
